```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Grist links tables with *reference* columns. A `Ref` column stores the row
`id` of a record in another table, and a `RefList` column stores several.
gristmillr returns these as integer row IDs, so there are three ways to bring
the related data together.

The examples use two tables: `People` (with a `name` column) and `Orders`
(with `item`, `qty` and a `person` column of type `Ref:People`).

```{r}
library(gristmillr)

doc <- grist_doc("<your document ID>")
```

## Look up display values

The Grist interface shows a reference as the value of a *display column*, such
as a person's name. `grist_resolve_refs()` looks those values up for data you
have already read:

```{r}
orders <- grist_records(doc, "Orders")

grist_resolve_refs(orders, doc, "Orders")
#>   id item person person_display qty
#> 1  1  pen      1           Ann   1
#> 2  2  ink      1           Ann   2
#> 3  3  pad      2           Bob   3
#> 4  4  cap     NA          <NA>   4
```

The original IDs are kept, so you can still join on them. Use
`how = "replace"` to swap the IDs for the display values, and `columns` to
choose which references to resolve. `RefList` columns become list-columns of
display values. If a reference has no display column in Grist, only the row IDs
exist, and the function warns and leaves the column alone.

## Join in R

When you need other columns from the related table, read both tables and join
on the reference. A `Ref` column matches the `id` column of the table it points
to, and an empty reference is `NA`.

```{r}
people <- grist_records(doc, "People")

merge(orders, people, by.x = "person", by.y = "id", all.x = TRUE,
      suffixes = c("", "_person"))

# With dplyr:
dplyr::left_join(orders, people, by = c(person = "id"), suffix = c("", "_person"))
```

For a `RefList` column, unnest it first, for example with
`tidyr::unnest_longer()`, and then join.

## Join in Grist with SQL

Grist documents are SQLite databases, so `grist_sql()` can join on the server
and return only the result. Use table IDs and column IDs as names. This is the
better choice for large tables or aggregates.

```{r}
grist_sql(
  doc,
  "select o.item, o.qty, p.name
   from Orders o
   left join People p on o.person = p.id
   order by o.id"
)

grist_sql(
  doc,
  "select p.name, sum(o.qty) as total
   from People p
   left join Orders o on o.person = p.id
   group by p.id"
)
```

SQL results carry no column types, so dates come back as numbers. Convert them
yourself, or use `grist_records()` when types matter.
